Omar: hey folks, Omar here. first day on Ubuntu 22.04 (Dell XPS). switched to fish shell. trying to bootstrap with asdf for python/node/go and run the dotfiles bootstrap. asdf fails compiling python 3.11 with an openssl/linker configure error. ssh-agent isn't starting for my user session (keys not available in VS Code). 1Password CLI prompts for SSO but I don't have vault access yet. who do I ping for Okta/vpn/git? any tips for apt build deps + fish?

Helena: welcome Omar :wave: on Ubuntu you usually need the build deps installed via apt before compiling Python. I keep a small script for new machines: 
```
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y build-essential libssl-dev zlib1g-dev libbz2-dev libreadline-dev libsqlite3-dev libffi-dev liblzma-dev pkg-config 
# for node/gpg imports
sudo apt install -y dirmngr gnupg
```
Then `asdf install python 3.11.6` should work. For Go just `asdf plugin add golang` + `asdf install golang 1.20.6`.

Helena: fish tips: ensure asdf is initialized in ~/.config/fish/config.fish: 
```
eval (asdf init - | source)
set -x PATH (asdf where)/shims $PATH
```
Also, if you run GUI editors from the launcher they don't read your login shell PATH; launch VS Code from terminal with `code .` or add a systemd user service to export the env for GUI sessions.

Omar: installed the apt deps and retried. python compiled 389. thanks! node failed at the gpg import step (gnupg was missing), installed that and re-ran import, node installed. ssh still not present inside VS Code though.

Helena: on modern Linux it's common to use a systemd user ssh-agent so the agent survives logins and is visible to GUI apps. Create `~/.config/systemd/user/ssh-agent.service` with the standard agent wrapper (or use keychain). Example snippet: 
```
[Service]
Type=forking
Environment=SSH_AUTH_SOCK=%t/ssh-agent.socket
ExecStart=/usr/bin/ssh-agent -a $SSH_AUTH_SOCK
[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
```
Then `systemctl --user enable --now ssh-agent` and add your key with `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`. That makes the socket available to VS Code and other GUI apps.

DevX: another GUI workaround: add `export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ssh-agent.socket` to your ~/.profile so desktop sessions pick it up. We prefer the systemd user unit for reproducibility.

ITSupport: Omar  for Okta/VPN/Git access open an IT ticket at https://itsupport.redwood.internal/new or reply here with your manager's email and employee id and we'll expedite. Typical ETA 1 business day.

dev_onboard_bot: Created checklist for Omar: [create-ssh-key, add-to-1password, install-apt-deps, install-asdf-runtimes, enable-ssh-agent-systemd, request-vpn] (0/6).

Omar: created ticket #ONB-214 and posted manager email in the ticket. also added the systemd unit and restarted user services 60a. ssh-agent socket now present and VS Code terminal sees the key.

Helena: for 1Password, once IT/PeopleOps add you to the org you'll get an Okta SSO invite. after that run `eval (op signin redwood --output=env)` in fish. don't commit any secrets; we keep a `secrets.sample` in the handbook and ask you to create `~/.redwood/env.local` for overrides.

Omar: got the Okta invite and 1Password access. everything green now — apt deps, asdf runtimes, systemd ssh-agent, node/gpg fixed. huge thanks everyone! :raised_hands:

DevX: welcome aboard! quick note: prefer devcontainer when provided for services — consistent Linux images. if you need native GPU or low-level kernel deps, run locally. tag @DevX for any devcontainer issues.

Omar: cool, will use devcontainers by default. thanks again :heart:
